## Building Analytics Systems

A major part of my work involves designing and supporting analytics systems that make complex data usable. This includes data preparation workflows, reproducible research pipelines, dashboard back ends, and structured datasets that support repeated analysis over time. My focus is not only on producing one off results, but on creating systems that make analysis faster, more reliable, and easier to communicate.

Across research and applied settings, I have worked with large administrative datasets, public health data, labor market data, and geographically structured data. I frequently build workflows that connect raw source files to cleaned intermediate datasets, and then to final analytic outputs such as statistical models, dashboards, maps, and reports.

## What I Mean by Data Systems

For me, data systems work includes several connected layers:

### Data acquisition and integration

This includes pulling data from multiple sources, standardizing identifiers, reconciling metadata, harmonizing time and geography, and preparing datasets for analysis. Many of my projects involve combining separate files or source systems into a single integrated analytic dataset.

### Reproducible transformation pipelines

I typically structure projects so that raw data, processing logic, and outputs are clearly separated. This allows datasets to be refreshed, updated, and reused without rebuilding the entire project manually. In several recent projects, I used dedicated preparation scripts to transform source data into parquet based analytic datasets for efficient downstream use.

### Analytics applications and dashboards

I build front end analytic tools that sit on top of prepared datasets, allowing users to explore trends, compare units, and interpret results without needing to work directly with raw data. These tools often include filtering, comparison views, mapped outputs, or statistical summaries designed for operational interpretation.

### Communication ready outputs

A useful analytics system should make it easier to communicate results. My workflows often support dashboards, reports, maps, and publication ready summaries from the same underlying prepared data resources.

## Recent Examples

### Labor market analytics system

In the JOLTS State Explorer project, I built a workflow that downloads raw BLS JOLTS source files, combines the core time series file with metadata tables, produces a processed monthly state level parquet dataset, and serves that dataset through an interactive Shiny for Python dashboard with both single state and comparison views. This is a good example of an end to end public data product built around a reusable processing layer and a lightweight exploration interface.

### County health spatial analytics system

In the County Health Explorer project, I integrated County Health Rankings & Roadmaps data, CDC PLACES indicators, and Census geography resources into a county level analytic system joined by FIPS code. The resulting application supports interactive mapping and local spatial autocorrelation analysis, showing how an integrated data backend can support both descriptive and inferential exploration in a single tool.

## Technical Orientation

My technical work is centered on building analytic systems that are clear, reproducible, and extensible. Depending on the project, this includes:

- R, Python, and SQL
- parquet based intermediate datasets
- geospatial data integration and mapping
- Shiny applications in R and Python
- Quarto based reporting and portfolio development
- model ready datasets for forecasting, spatial analysis, and statistical inference

## Relevance of my experience

For industry and analytics leadership roles, this work demonstrates that I can contribute across the lifecycle of a data product:

- framing the analytic problem
- designing the data structure needed to answer it
- building reusable processing workflows
- developing interactive products for stakeholders
- translating technical results into usable business or policy insight

This is the part of my background that connects academic rigor with production oriented analytics work. It shows not just that I can analyze data, but that I can help build the systems that make high quality analytics possible at scale.
